How feasible is it to send a probe like New Horizons to an exoplanet? How long would it take to get there and are there any plans in the works for such a thing?

Short answer: Not very.

Longer answer:

The fastest interplanetary spacecraft we have is Voyager 1. It moves along at around 60,000 km/h. Light travels more than 1,000,000,000 km/h. So, let's be charitable and say we could build a probe that goes 100,000 km/h. That is still only 0.01% of the speed of light.

The nearest exoplanet is at Alpha Centauri B. (Note that this planet has not yet been confirmed, so it may be considerably farther to the nearest one.) That is about 4.5 light years away. If it takes light 4.5 years, it would take our theoretically super-fast probe 45,000 years.

So, we could try to send something, but the chances of nothing going wrong or that we will even still be around when it gets there are pretty slim.
Wow, guess there's not really any chance of it happening during my life then. Thanks for the answer.

Unfortunately, you are right that the chances are very, very slim. However, never say never. New advances are being made all the time. There are multiple projects on faster then light travel. They are highly doubtful to be successful in the next 5-10 years, but 10-20? It gets very hard to predict that far out. That doesn't mean it will happen, it just means we don't know.
